payload.text:
I reviewed `upload-extensions` against `main`: two commits, the content-type lookup and filename sanitizing. I didn't edit anything. It shouldn't be merged yet, because the extension parsing is wrong for most real filenames.

**Blocker: `extensionOf` in `src/extension.js`**
It uses `name.split('.')[1]`, which takes the text after the *first* dot and doesn't lowercase it. The README says it should be the text after the *last* dot, lowercased. I ran it on the branch:

| Filename | Expected | Got | Content type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Archive.TAR.GZ` | `gz` | `TAR` | octet-stream ✗ |
| `photo.JPG` | `jpg` | `JPG` | octet-stream ✗ |
| `my.photo.jpg` | `jpg` | `photo` | octet-stream ✗ |
| `README` | `""` | `undefined` | octet-stream (only works because of the fallback) |
| `file.` | `""` | `""` | ✓ |

So any filename with uppercase letters or more than one dot gets `application/octet-stream`. A fix along these lines would work: `const i = name.lastIndexOf('.'); return i < 0 ? '' : name.slice(i + 1).toLowerCase();`

**Tests are too thin**
The only extension test is `photo.jpg`, which happens to pass with the buggy code. Add the README's own examples (`Archive.TAR.GZ`, `photo.JPG`), plus a multi-dot name, a name with no dot and a trailing dot. There are no tests for `contentType` at all.

**`safeName` is mostly fine, with one gap**
Slashes and backslashes anywhere in the name become `_`, so `a/../../b` turns into `a_.._.._b` and can't climb out of a directory. That part is sound. But `.`, `..` and `...` all become an **empty string**. If a caller joins that onto the upload directory, it points at the directory itself. It should either reject empty results or substitute a default name.

**Minor**
- The CHANGELOG entry for 0.5.0 doesn't mention safe names.
- Exporting `TYPES` lets other code change the shared lookup table. Freeze it or don't export it.

The version bump and README wording look fine.
